scope: Proposition 7.4 (Radial cutoffs) of the manuscript “Arithmeticity of twisted finite correspondences for lattices over local fields” (preprints/Arithmeticity-of-twisted-finite-correspondences-for-lattices-over-local-fields-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 286 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b1d070a5c4cd8496), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 66-67. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let f ∈ C∞([0, ∞)) be constant on a neighborhood of zero and on a neighborhood of infinity. There are Rf , Cf > 0 such that the kernel (x, x′ ) 7−→ f(d(x, x′ )/R) has Schur multiplier norm at most Cf for every R ≥ Rf . Consequently, if a countable group Γ has any homomorphism into Isom(X), η is a normalized scalar cocycle, and B is a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, then Df(r/R) : B ¯ ⊗Lη(Γ) −→ B ¯ ⊗Lη(Γ), X h Yhuh 7−→ X h f(r(h)/R)Yhuh ARITHMETICITY OF TWISTED FINITE CORRESPONDENCES 67 has completely bounded norm at most Cf . The constants are independent of Γ, η, B and of the homomorphism.
